title: Sec Eng: case log + threat handoff (2026-04-13)
content:
Security Engineering sync — case log and threat handoff
Date: 2026-04-13 (notes compiled & distributed 2026-04-14)
Owner / recorder: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha Patel, Marco Ruiz, Ling Chen, Riley Thompson, Zoe Martinez
Apologies: N/A
Duration: 45m
Meeting purpose: Consolidate active vuln cases for handoff to on-call and infra, review recent secrets exposure, finalize threat-model follow-ups for hosted API rollout, and identify playbook changes.

Agenda:
1) Quick status: open vuln queue and priority changes
2) Case deep-dive (three high-touch items)
3) Secrets incident summary and permanent mitigations
4) Threat modeling actionables for hosted API changes (short-lived tokens, egress rules)
5) Playbook edits and on-call handoff
6) AOB / open questions

---
1) Quick status
- Current open vuln tickets (SECV-*): 27 total; 6 high (P1/P2), 14 medium, 7 low. We are prioritizing by customer-impacted + exploitability.
- Notable: SECV-4123 (see case below) escalated to P1 for potential public key leakage vector.

2) Case deep-dive
A) SECV-4123 — CICD artifact logs leaking ephemeral credentials (P1) - Discovered: 2026-04-11 by automated secret scanner (internal tool) during upstream push to infra/cicd repo.
- Affected components: infra-builders CI jobs (builder-aws-prod); potentially used short-lived IAM roles for deployment.
- Risk: high — ephemeral creds persisted in build logs uploaded to internal S3 with public-read misconfiguration for a subset of objects.
- Exploitability: medium-high (requires scanning public S3 listings or known bucket keys, but we do not currently believe it was harvested).
- Immediate mitigation performed: revoked affected temporary roles and rotated the two service principal tokens reported in logs; tightened the S3 object ACLs to private. (Owner: Marco Ruiz)
- Follow-ups: update CI to redact tokens from logs (add redaction wrapper to build steps), add post-build scanner that rejects uploads with credentials, and schedule a retro with build-team.
- Tickets: SECV-4123 (P1), INFRA-2197 (ci-redaction), ACTION: Marco Ruiz — patch to redaction wrapper by 2026-04-18; Ling Chen — add S3 policy enforcement to infra policy engine by 2026-04-22.

B) SECV-4150 — model-serving HTTP header reflection / info leak (P2) - Discovered: fuzzing run by QA (2026-04-09). Some debug headers leaked internal shard ids and partial KV cache sizes when a malformed request was sent to older v1 endpoints.
- Affected components: legacy serving-runtime v1 (edge variants).
- Risk: medium (information disclosure could assist targeted probing).
- Mitigation: disabled v1 endpoints for public routes and applied header-sanitization middleware to all gateways. (Owner: Ling Chen)
- Follow-ups: mandatory test in regression suite for header-sanitization; risk review for v1 removal schedule. Ticket: SECV-4150 (P2), TEST-879 (regression). ACTION: Ling Chen — add regression by 2026-04-20; Product to confirm deprecation timeline.

C) SECV-4168 — insufficient RBAC on internal prompt-eval tool (P2) - Discovered: internal audit (2026-04-12). Prompt-eval UI was reachable by a stale oauth client scope allowing cross-team reading of eval prompts (could contain customer PII in some test cases).
- Affected components: prompt-eval webapp (internal only).
- Risk: medium-high for regulated customers.
- Mitigation: revoked stale client, tightened scope checks, limited access to sec-eng and product-evals team pending hardening. (Owner: Zoe Martinez)
- Follow-ups: add automated periodic client scope audit, add alert when eval prompts include customer identifiers, update onboarding docs. Ticket: SECV-4168 (P2). ACTION: Zoe Martinez — automated audit script by 2026-04-25; Product/legal to provide redaction guidance by 2026-04-21.

3) Secrets incident summary & permanent mitigations
Summary of recent exposures (last 30d): two transient exposures (one CI log, one internal slack paste) both contained short-lived tokens — rotated immediately; no confirmed external access.
Root causes observed: 1) lack of log redaction in custom build steps; 2) manual copy/paste into channels by engineers.
Permanent mitigations agreed:
- CI hardening: centralized redaction library, fail-build on token patterns, S3 upload policy enforcement. (INFRA-2197)
- Slack/GDrive guidance: short micro-education + mandatory automated DLP on shared_drives for patterns that look like keys. (Security Ops / Comms)
- Short-lived credentials adoption: move more teams to ephemeral KMS-derived tokens and reduce TTLs from 1h to 10m for sensitive deploy flows. Product/Infra to measure perf impact.
Owners and timelines: Marco (CI redaction) 2026-04-18; Ling (policy enforcement) 2026-04-22; Security Ops (DLP rollout) 2026-05-05.

4) Threat modeling follow-ups (hosted API + rollout changes)
Context: Product plans to increase per-route feature flags for model fallback (auto-fallback to quantized variants) and introduce a new streaming gateway that aggregates responses across regions. We need to ensure threat-model decisions cover token handling, egress, and fallback behavior.
Decisions / actionables from meeting:
- Short-lived endpoint tokens: require Product and SDKs to support 5–15 minute tokens for streaming sessions. (Owner: Riley Thompson; ACTION by 2026-04-26).
- Egress allowlist tightening: block unexpected long-tail egress destinations from dedicated/private nodes; infra to add egress policy that defaults to deny and allow only approved domains for model telemetry. (Owner: Ling Chen; ACTION by 2026-04-30).
- Fallback policy safety net: when fallback occurs to quantized variant, OTel trace must include a non-sensitive flag, and customer-configured rollout policy must be visible in console (no PII in traces). Product to add console UI note. (Owner: Product-eng lead, noted in linked_artifacts).
- Streaming gateway: threat-model reviewer to produce mini-RMF (risk matrix) for new gateway by next sync; include replay/sequence injection scenarios and mitigations (HMAC per chunk, sequence numbers). (Owner: Marco Ruiz; DUE 2026-04-27).

5) Playbook / runbook edits
- Add a short checklist to the Secrets Handling Playbook: immediate rotation + CI redaction check + communication template. (Owner: Zoe Martinez; PR to confluence by 2026-04-19).
- Update the Vulnerability Triage Playbook to include a P1 readiness ladder for public bucket exposures (quick checklist for S3 ACLs, CloudTrail evidence collection). (Owner: Aisha Patel; PR by 2026-04-21).

6) Action items (consolidated)
- Marco Ruiz — implement and land CI redaction wrapper + unit tests. Ticket INFRA-2197. Due 2026-04-18.
- Ling Chen — add S3 policy enforcement to infra policy engine; add header-sanitization regression test. Tickets INFRA-2201 / TEST-879. Due 2026-04-22 and 2026-04-20 respectively.
- Zoe Martinez — Confluence edits to Secrets Playbook + automated client-audit script for prompt-eval. Due 2026-04-19 (playbook) and 2026-04-25 (audit script).
- Riley Thompson — prototype short-lived token flow for streaming SDK; design doc PR. Due 2026-04-26.
- Aisha Patel — update Vulnerability Triage Playbook to include public-bucket checklist; coordinate incident retro. Due 2026-04-21.
- Product lead (cc: Product-eng) — confirm v1 deprecation timeline and add console note for fallback visibility. Requested by 2026-04-20.

7) On-call handoff note
- Current P1 (SECV-4123) remains active and is escalated to on-call for the upcoming weekend. Marco will be primary; Riley backup. If new evidence of external access is found, page on-call PD and notify Legal.

8) Retrospective snippets (quick)
- What went well: automated secret scanner caught CI leak before external exposure.
- Improvement: need better pre-commit hooks / build-step linting for secrets patterns; also we should provide a short, visible guidance for engineers about paste hygiene.

9) Open questions and risks
- Do we need to accelerate migration to ephemeral tokens for all production deploys? (Cost/latency tradeoffs — infra team to model.)
- Full audit coverage for GDrive shared_drives — ETA for DLP rollout from Security Ops? (Security Ops to confirm 2026-05-05).
- Is there appetite to retire legacy v1 serving-runtime earlier given the pattern of header leaks? Product to advise.

Next sync: 2026-04-20, 10:00am PT (weekly cadence). Will focus on progress on actionables and any new evidence on SECV-4123.

Appendix: quick references
- SECV-4123: CI log leak ticket (details, redaction patches, evidence bucket listing)
- Confluence: Secrets Handling Playbook — https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Secrets-Handling-Playbook
- Threat model catalog: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Sec/Threat+Model+Catalog
- Infra PR for initial redaction lib: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/892

Notes to self: include a short 'how to escalate' one-pager in the next playbook update (what to say to legal, when to page infra).
